### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os db orphans (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts), os secret orphans (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os secret orphans (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via os db orphans (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0bbe71bb8cdda1cbd22a138c27ac6e7aae33869d` — the merge of head `f5ade533679be6d88e133529ed4f9e6516bba24f` into base `0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0bbe71bb8cdda1cbd22a138c27ac6e7aae33869d && git checkout 0bbe71bb8cdda1cbd22a138c27ac6e7aae33869d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a f5ade533679be6d88e133529ed4f9e6516bba24f && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a && git merge --no-ff f5ade533679be6d88e133529ed4f9e6516bba24f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d727b70716ccf77fd63d0a0a2f0b17f7ab4d28a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### Checklist
- Shape: open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36331`; no closing keyword binds another card. `Fixes` is right: the three Done-when lines are delivered (text face non-TTY exit 1 naming `--yes` in both commands, the interactive decline kept at exit 0 as the migrate family does, a sibling pin over both commands with an ablation: 2 red at `origin/main` sources, restored to the HEAD blobs).

- Pin: the roster case reads the command classes' flags (`delete` + `yes`) so a third such command fails until it has a row; `process.stdin.isTTY` is set per run; deletes and export writes are observed on fakes.
- Gates at this head: Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`; all checks 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### REWORK items
1. **The narrowing is undeclared.** The text face's exit status goes from `0` to `1` for the same invocation. The card's own named precedent, `os migrate apply` (`62bc129` in `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md`), made exactly this change and declared it as `fix(cli)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, an `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and a **BREAKING** (an exit status narrows) banner with FROM / TO / Unchanged / the fix for a script. This PR carries a bare `Clause-②: no`, no `!`, no banner and no marker. Fix in the changeset body and the PR body/title, following that precedent: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `!` in the title and changeset headline, the BREAKING banner (FROM: `--delete` without `--yes`, stdin not a terminal, text face: nothing deleted, exit `0`; TO: same, exit `1`, the new `Confirmation required…` line; Unchanged: `n` at the prompt exits `0`, `--json` already exited `1`; the fix for a script: pass `--yes`), and the `adr-0087` marker. Run `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` again after the edit. No code change is asked.
2. **Owed once the arm is declared:** the dogfood battery in full, pinned to the new head (`dogfood_battery` in the report), and a contract review on the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, which this review thread runs on the new head.

Reach read from source only. Left to the seat's filing gate, as one family-close card that also widens the pin population to apply-behind-`--yes` modes outside `migrate`.
- The report's API reads and gate readings were checked against this head; no git-answerable API read to note.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ca5b49ee6dacd0298534cc5191d411c8fe7caa43`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts, packages/cli/test/orphans-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/** (the `--yes` gates, `apply.ts` and `list-preferences.ts` in full at the gate), packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts (`printWarning`, `emitJson`, `isExitSignal`), packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/deploy.ts with packages/cli/src/utils/terminal-confirm.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.guards.test.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md (entry 62bc129), content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx

Read on this head: the net diff against `main` (4 files, +367/-0), card #36331 with all five comments, the PR body and its five comments, and the check-runs on this head (0 failed, 0 pending; skipped runs are the path-filtered UI, docs and opt-in jobs).

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no change. No flag, argument, value or `--json` document key is added, removed or re-typed in either command. Right as declared (`Clause-②: no`).
- Public surface, exit status: one narrowing, the same in both commands. `--delete` without `--yes`, text face, `process.stdin.isTTY` falsy, with at least one row to delete: exit `0` becomes exit `1`. The new branch sits inside `if (!flags.yes)`, after the `--json` branch and before `confirm()`, in `db/orphans.ts` and `secret/orphans.ts` alike. Declared as `(narrowing)`: right.
- Public surface, printed line: on that same path `Aborted — no export was written and no row was deleted.` (info) becomes `Confirmation required. Re-run with --yes to delete. No export was written and no row was deleted.` (warning, stdout), each followed by the journal-mode note when the target is a SQLite file. The changeset quotes the new line exactly. Right.
- Unchanged, each read in the tree and each right: the `--json` face (`confirmation_required`, exit 1, already so on `main`); a terminal answered `n` (`Aborted — …`, plain return, exit 0); `--yes` (the gate is skipped whole); nothing to delete (returns before the gate, exit 0, no prompt); `--delete` without `--export`, an existing export path and the secret union refusal (all exit 1 before the gate, untouched).
- Nothing is written on the refused path: the new branch exits before the export block in both files, so "writes no export, deletes nothing" holds. `this.exit(1)` is thrown inside the `try` whose `catch` rethrows on `isExitSignal` and whose `finally` shuts the stack down, in both files, so the exit is not rewritten to `scan_failed` and the stack is closed.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/cli': patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No spec key, authorable value or stored shape moves. The level axis in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` on `main` grades a `none` change `patch`, "`fix!:` alike", and says a non-protocol change keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition at `patch`. The precedent's `minor` (62bc129) was the launch-window convention that axis replaced; following it here would be refused. `Check Changeset`: success on this head.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right, and present on both the PR body and the changeset. The title and the changeset headline carry `!`, and the BREAKING banner carries FROM / TO / Unchanged / the fix for a script, the precedent's shape.
- FROM / TO / Unchanged against the tree: FROM matches `main` (`confirm()` answers `false` when stdin is no terminal, then `Aborted — …` and a plain return). TO matches the head. All four Unchanged clauses hold (① above). The headline's claim about the `os migrate` family holds: every `--yes` gate under `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/**` exits 1 on the non-interactive text face.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. Nothing exists for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the remedy is a flag on the caller's command line. The marker is the precedent's, with "one CLI command" correctly changed to "two CLI commands". `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates`: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both reports. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, level kept at `patch` against the dispatch's "follow the precedent's level": accepted, see ②.
- Deviations on the commit trailer and the PR-body footer and signature: process only, no effect on the contract; `PR-body guards` success.
- Deviation, five gate families not measured locally for missing prerequisites: answered by the head's check-runs, all success.
- Dogfood battery owed by the `(narrowing)` arm: the dev reports a full run at this head with 0 failures. That is the dev's reading, not re-run here. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run on this head is success; its shards were skipped by the path filter.
- Out-of-scope finding, `os secret rewrap --apply` (same gate shape, text face exits 0 when stdin is no terminal): confirmed in the tree at `secret/rewrap.ts`. It is outside this card and is carried by open card #36679. Not escalated further.
- Docs: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` states no exit status for a refused confirmation, and `-y, --yes — skip the confirmation prompt` stays true. No file under `skills/` names either command. `Skills-docs: none` is right.
- SQL push-down: no new query, id materialisation or in-app join. The two source hunks add one branch on `process.stdin.isTTY`; the pin runs on fakes.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- The narrowing takes no declared capability away. Nothing on `main` declares exit 0 for an unconfirmed `--delete`: the flag text says `--yes` skips the prompt, the `--json` flag says deleting "requires --yes", and `cli.mdx` is silent on the status. The refusal was already real (nothing exported, nothing deleted); the status and the line now report it. The capability a script loses is reading a no-op as success, which was the defect. A script that means to delete passes `--yes`; one that wants the report drops `--delete`. Both remedies work on this head.
- Agreement with the `os migrate` rule: exact. `migrate/list-preferences.ts` has the same three-step gate (`--json` exits 1; stdin no terminal warns naming `--yes` and `this.exit(1)`; the prompt's `n` prints `Aborted — …` and returns 0), and `migrate/apply.ts` words its line the same way. `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` pins exit 1 on both faces and keeps the decline at exit 0 as a control. This PR copies that rule and widens nothing beyond it.
- Tried to break it, and it held: (a) a non-interactive run cannot reach the prompt or the export, since the branch precedes both; (b) the exit signal is not swallowed, since both `catch` blocks rethrow it; (c) the pin cannot pass vacuously on an unrelated exit 1, since the `--yes` control uses the same fixtures and argv, deletes exactly one row and writes the export; (d) the pin sets `process.stdin.isTTY` per run and restores it; (e) the existing `secret/orphans.guards.test.ts` decline case runs on a terminal, so it does not contradict the change; (f) `--yes` on stdin no terminal still deletes.
- The pin exercises both commands and both faces. Per command: text face (exit 1, output names `--yes`, no delete, no export file, no prompt), `--json` face (exit 1, `confirmation_required`, no delete, no export), `--yes` control (exit 0, one delete, export written) and terminal `n` control (one prompt, exit 0, nothing deleted). The dev's ablation, both sources restored to `main`, turned exactly the two text-face cases red. `Test Core` 10/10: success.
- Same gate shape elsewhere in the CLI: one escape, `os secret rewrap --apply`, pre-existing, outside this diff, on card #36679. No other command outside `migrate/**` declares a `yes` flag. `os deploy` asks through `terminal-confirm.ts` in a different shape (no `--yes`, a decline exits 1) and is not this family.
- nit — the pin's population reads only modules one directory below `src/commands` and pre-filters on the source text `delete: Flags.boolean` and `yes: Flags.boolean`. A top-level command module, a nested topic such as `plugin/trust/*`, or a flag declared through a quoted key or a shared flag set would not join the roster, so the header's "a third such command fails here" holds only for that reach. No such module exists today. Left as a follow-up: fold it into #36679, which already widens the population to apply-behind-`--yes` modes. A fix in this PR would move the head.
- nit — on the refused path the line `About to permanently delete N row(s) … The export below is the only copy that survives.` still prints before `Confirmation required …`. It was so before this change and each line is true on its own. Accepted deviation.
